newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb badly damages tax office in southern France.
newsitem.headline: Bomb badly damages tax office in southern France.

text.p: A powerful bomb exploded at a tax office in the southern French city of Perpignan early on Tuesday, badly damaging the front of the building but causing no injuries, local officials said.
No one claimed responsibility for the blast, which went off shortly before 1 a.m. (2400 GMT on Monday).
Police initally suspected Corsican separatists or radical sympathisers of the Confederation for the Defence of Shop Owners and Artisans (CDCA), a right-wing shop owners' union.

French police fired tear gas into the air in nearby Montpellier on Monday during clashes with several hundred people protesting at the detention of a CDCA union leader there on suspicion of corruption.
Corsican separatists seeking greater autonomy for the Mediterranean resort island have carried their guerrilla campaign to mainland France in recent months and frequently target public buildings.
